attributes.body:
In order to express that you will (or someone else should) try something, the conjunction particle て will be paired with 見（み）る (almost always without kanji). While this is translated as 'to try to (A)', the actual meaning is closer to 'to do (A), and see (whether the result is good or not)'.

This grammar construction is usually only used when someone tries something for the first time.

As mentioned above, this phrase is also used when suggesting that someone else should try something. In these situations, (A) + てみて, or more formally, (A) + てみてください will be used.

Sometimes, in very casual requests, even the て of みて will be dropped, and (A) + てみ will be used by itself. This usually has the nuance of 'come on, just give it a go!'

Caution

When てみた appears in the past tense, it will imply that the attempt was successful, unless specifically stated otherwise by the speaker.

Fun Fact

While the kanji for 見（み）る may be used in this grammar point, it will result in the 'see' meaning being heavily stressed (rather than 'try'). This may cause a misunderstanding on the part of the person listening/reading.

attributes.description: verb[て]みる vs verb[volitional]とする

attributes.body: てみる expresses trying something to see what it's like, similar to the English 'try (doing)', e.g. 食べてみる ('I'll try eating it.'). てごらん is a more directive form that encourages someone else to try something, e.g. 食べてごらん ('Try eating it.' as a gentle request). てごらん is often used by adults to children, or superiors to subordinates. Among peers, something like 食べてみて would be more common.

Both can be translated in English as 'try (doing)', but differ in nuance. ようにする means to make an effort or form a habit, e.g. 毎朝走るようにしている ('I try to run every morning.') has the nuance of making a point of doing so. In contrast, てみる means to try something out to see the result, e.g. 走ってみた ('I tried running.'), which has the nuance of doing so to see what it was like.

first_relatable.title: ようにする
first_relatable.meaning: To try to, To make sure to, To endeavor to

attributes.body: Verb[volitional]とする and てみる are both translated as 'try', but the former implies attempting something that may not succeed, e.g. 話そうとした ('I tried to speak.'), which implies that maybe the attempt was unsuccessful. In contrast,てみる focuses on trying something to see the result, as in 話してみた ('I tried speaking.'), which has the nuance of doing so to see what it was like.

first_relatable.title: Verb[volitional]とする
first_relatable.meaning: Try to, Attempt to, To be about to

attributes.body: 〜ようと思う・〜おうと思う expresses intention, similar to 'I'm thinking of doing X,' e.g. 行こうと思います ('I plan to go.') てみる conveys the idea of trying something to see what it's like, e.g. 行ってみる ('I'll go and see.'). These forms can be combined, e.g. 行ってみようと思います ('I plan to go and see what it's like.')
